column1: # How the 431 genomes of the extended reference set were chosen, from the 454 dereplicated
# representatives of the mashID Brucella pack's source collection (figshare article 33970168, version 4;
# 2,022 NCBI taxon-234 assemblies, dereplicated at a MASH distance of 0.0003).
# Validated on simulated reads of all 2,022 assemblies: 1543/1543 held-out samples of a named species
# right once the five mislabelled truth genomes below are accounted for -- the five EXCLUDE rows whose
# reason is a contradicted label, not the two excluded for being too far from the clade to be a
# reference at all (wiki, Validation), nor GCA_040391195.1, excluded for being two fifths of a genome.
# Every genome not listed here was kept as it was.
# The DROP-SP cutoff of 0.004 was set on the classical species and does not transfer: it dropped three
# genomes that are not twins at all. GCA_000163135.1 is B. papionis (now a RELABEL), and
# GCA_030157885.1 and GCA_000370945.1 are distinct unnamed lineages, outside the diversity of the
# species they were said to duplicate, so both are kept. curation/mislabelled_records.md shows the
# measurements. A genome is a twin here only when it sits inside its neighbour species' own spread.
# Species assignment in the former Ochrobactrum part of the clade is by ANI to the TYPE STRAIN of each
# species, not by Mash distance to the nearest neighbouring genome -- but a type-strain comparison does
# not settle it on its own, because four pairs in this group are inseparable (below), and inside such a
# pair the senior name has priority. Both of the records this bears on are relabelled, and both rest on
# priority rather than on the nearest type strain:
#   GCA_049065255.1 (SA289) is 99.09% ANI to the ciceri type strain and 98.35% to the intermedia type.
#   Read as a type-strain comparison alone that looks like ciceri, but the two are one species by the
#   95% criterion, intermedia (Velasco 1998) is senior to ciceri (Imran 2010), and 11 of the 12 genomes
#   in its own cluster are deposited as intermedia. It is intermedia.
#   GCA_059995225.1 (WTB2) is 99.11% to the lupini type, 96.87% to anthropi and 95.65% to cytisi -- all
#   one species -- so it carries the senior name, anthropi (1988).
# curation/mislabelled_records.md sets out both, and references_extended.tsv carries both labels.
# Four pairs of named species in this group have type strains at or above 95% ANI and so are not
# separable by the standard criterion: intermedia/ciceri 98.26%, anthropi/lupini 97.14%, lupini/cytisi
# 95.95%, anthropi/cytisi 95.51%. Within those groups a species label is partly a nomenclatural choice,
# and this file does not try to settle one.
# The records whose label the sequence contradicts are tracked, with the evidence for each, in
# curation/mislabelled_records.md, so they can be reported to the submitters and to NCBI.

strain 141012304 is 97.87% ANI and 0.0212 from the inopinata type strain BO1, further than three references the set calls Brucella sp. (BO2 98.24%, 2280 98.08%, BO3 98.01%); the other inopinata genome, GCA_030270765.1, is 99.88% and 0.0017 from BO1. ANI cannot assign species in the classical clade, where every genome clears 95% against every type strain, so this rests on the relative comparison. Its nearest genome of the set is 0.0158 away, and no other of the 2,022 assemblies is within 0.005 of it; curation/unnamed_lineages.md

strain NM4 is 99.17% ANI to the Ochrobactrum soli type strain BO-7 and 98.15% to the O. teleogrylli type CGMCC 1.13984; the nearest type of a named Brucella species is haematophila CIP 109452, about 90%. The species is Ochrobactrum teleogrylli Hu et al. 2020: the soli and teleogrylli type strains are 98.16% ANI apart, so one species, and teleogrylli was validly published first (IJSEM 2020; soli was validated in 2024). NCBI files it under Ochrobactrum, outside taxon 234, and no Brucella combination exists, so the set carries the name as published; curation/unnamed_lineages.md

a partial genome: 2.1 Mb of a species of about 5 Mb. It is Ochrobactrum teleogrylli by ANI (98.90% to the O. soli type strain BO-7 and 98.53% to the O. teleogrylli type, on 636 and 629 of 686 fragments) and was briefly carried under that name, but a reference holding two fifths of its genome cannot be matched closely by a complete library of its own species, and none did: it was the best match of no run among 4,024 public read sets, ranking third at 301 to 362 of 1000 hashes for the three O. teleogrylli runs, behind GCA_030063905.1 and GCA_040372265.1, which carry the species. Removing it changes the call of no public run and of no simulated sample but its own; curation/unnamed_lineages.md
